stem.en: Boiling points: water 100 °C, acetone 56 °C, alcohol 78 °C, chloroform 61 °C, benzene 80 °C. Mixtures: (i) water and acetone, (ii) water and salt, (iii) acetone and alcohol, (iv) sand and salt, (v) alcohol and chloroform, (vi) alcohol and benzene. Which can simple distillation separate?

explanation.en: Water and acetone are 44 °C apart, so (i) works. In (ii), water distils off and the salt stays behind. Choosing (i) alone forgets that distillation also gets a liquid from a solution. Acetone and alcohol are 22 °C apart, below about 25 °C, and (v) and (vi) are closer still. Sand and salt are two solids with no liquid to boil off.

hints.en: Work out each gap by subtraction. Which pairs are about 25 °C apart or more?
Distillation can also get a liquid from a solution. Is there a mixture like that in the list?
